paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The LORD doesn't look away from how people treat each other. He names the needy being sold for "a pair of sandals" and the poor being trampled (Amos 2:6-7). And the same people lay down beside every altar on garments taken in pledge, and drank wine obtained through fines in the house of their God (Amos 2:8). How we treat people matters to Him, and worship can't cover it up.

Now look at what the LORD says He did first. He destroyed the Amorite, tall as the cedars, and He brought Israel up from Egypt and led them forty years in the wilderness (Amos 2:9-10). He raised up prophets and Nazirites too (Amos 2:11). Everything Israel had, it had because of Him. Then Israel made the Nazirites drink wine and commanded the prophets not to prophesy (Amos 2:12). Friend, when the LORD sends a word, silencing the messenger doesn't change the message!

So what do I do with this, baker? I listen when His Word speaks, even when it steps on my toes. I'm a stamper who got pulled out of a junk drawer, so believe me, I know I didn't earn a thing I have. The LORD says that on that day the swift, the strong and the mighty can't save themselves (Amos 2:14-16). Our safety was never in our own strength, and that's good news for anyone who leans on Him instead.
